definitions.gloss: to jump at; to pounce on
definitions.explanation: To physically leap onto someone or something.

definitions.gloss: to jump at; to eagerly seize
definitions.explanation: To eagerly accept an offer or opportunity without hesitation.

examples.english: The cat pounced on its prey.

examples.japanese: ⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦たち→達：01551_tachi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦お{菓子|かし}→お菓子：02852_okashi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{飛|と}び{付|つ}いた。
examples.english: The children pounced on the sweets.

examples.japanese: ⟦{犬|いぬ}→犬：00632_inu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{帰|かえ}ってきた→帰る：00508_kaeru⟧⟦{飼|か}い{主|ぬし}→飼い主：15281_kainushi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{飛|と}び{付|つ}いた。
examples.english: The dog jumped on its owner who had just come home.

examples.japanese: ⟦チャンス→チャンス：03857_chansu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{飛|と}び{付|つ}く。
⟦そんな→そんな：01645_sonna⟧⟦{怪|あや}しい→怪しい：10267_ayashii⟧⟦{話|はなし}→話：01496_hanashi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦すぐ→すぐ：00814_sugu⟧{飛|と}び{付|つ}いて⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦いけない→いけない：02335_ikenai⟧。
examples.english: You shouldn't jump at such a suspicious offer.

examples.japanese: ⟦{安|やす}い→安い：00464_yasui⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧といって{飛|と}び{付|つ}くと、⟦{後|あと}→後：09580_ato⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{後悔|こうかい}→後悔：02738_koukai⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦こと→こと：01164_koto⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: If you eagerly jump at something just because it's cheap, you may regret it later.

notes:
FORMS:
Compound verb: ⟦{飛|と}ぶ→飛ぶ：00759_tobu⟧ (to jump, to fly) + ⟦{付|つ}く→付く：01960_tsuku⟧ (to attach, to stick)

TRANSITIVITY:
⟦{自動詞|じどうし}→自動詞：10977_jidoushi⟧ (intransitive). The target takes ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧, never ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧:
- X⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{飛|と}び{付|つ}く (to jump at X)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{話|はなし}→話：01496_hanashi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{飛|と}び{付|つ}く (to jump at an offer)
- ⟦{獲物|えもの}→獲物：08638_emono⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{飛|と}び{付|つ}く (to pounce on prey)
- ⟦チャンス→チャンス：03857_chansu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{飛|と}び{付|つ}く (to seize an opportunity)

USAGE:
Sense 1 is a single sudden movement ending in contact, so it is normally reported in the past ({飛|と}び{付|つ}いた) rather than as an ongoing action. Used figuratively (sense 2), it carries clear disapproval: the person grabbed the offer too fast to think it through, which is why it so often appears in warnings (examples 5 and 6).
